coverage_notes:
Pooled 56 candidates -> final 37 deduped rows, weighted to T1/T2 (1 T0, 14 T1, 9 T2, 13 T3). subdomain=anatomy for all.

DEDUP/DROPS: (1) UW Radiology gluteus-maximus + gastrocnemius and TeachMeAnatomy encyclopaedia gluteus-maximus + infraspinatus dropped as redundant single-muscle pages — same origin/insertion/innervation template already covered by Kenhub muscle pages and TeachMeAnatomy regional hubs. (2) Royal Society Interface biarticular review dropped: WebFetch returned 403 and license stayed unknown; superseded by the CC-BY PMC two-joint-link review (PMC9681132). (3) OpenStax 11-chapter-review folded into the richer OpenStax 11.4/11.6/11.1 pages (thin overview, no unique rows). (4) Physiopedia Gastrocnemius, Cardinal-Planes, ExRx LatissimusDorsi, Kenhub glute-max/biceps/quads/gastro singles, Beardsley Medium synthesis, and several secondary primary papers (PMC8219857 Nordic, PMC3003754 rabbit sarcomere, PMC11708772 knee-position MG, PMC7765981 multi-joint plantarflexor, PMC4221557 hip-flexor length-EMG, pubmed 12223171 gastroc knee-flexor, PMC8174684 triceps elbow-angle, PMC6047503 curl variants, PMC449729 lat weight-training, pubmed 24462394 lat isometric, koreascience triceps, Sage Sports Health lat HD-sEMG, sandcresearch) were de-prioritized as redundant — each contested claim already retains 1-2 strongest, openly-licensed primaries plus a textbook/atlas authority, which satisfies the PLAN's "two independent authorities per contested fact" bar without bloating the registry past the 15-28 target band quality-weight.

LICENSE CONFIRMED: PMC8191471 = CC BY 4.0 (fetched). Tandfonline triceps RCT and Sage lat paper unconfirmable -> Tandf kept as reference-only (it is the unique primary for triceps-overhead so retained); Sage lat paper dropped (lat regionalization already covered by PMC11057623 + PMC12452428, both CC BY). Wikipedia pages = CC BY-SA -> redistribute-ok. StatPearls (NBK*) hosted on NCBI but copyrighted -> reference-only. Physiopedia/Kenhub/TeachMeAnatomy/ExRx proprietary -> reference-only (store metadata + paraphrase, no copied figures).

NAMED-AUTHORITY COVERAGE (all PLAN authorities represented): Kenhub (hip/thigh, pec major, gastroc), Physiopedia (lat, active/passive insufficiency), TeachMeAnatomy (upper-limb hub, ant/post forearm, upper arm, gluteal, ant thigh, hamstrings), OpenStax A&P (11.1/11.4/11.6 + OSU + LibreTexts OERI mirrors w/ innervation), ExRx (hamstrings), StatPearls (shoulder, rectus femoris). Neumann 'Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System' and NSCA Essentials are PRINT-ONLY (no fetchable canonical URL existed in the pool) — their muscle-attachment/kinesiology function is covered by the open A&P texts (OpenStax/LibreTexts/OSU) + StatPearls; record Neumann/NSCA as offline citations in Phase B if a print copy is available, otherwise the OA texts suffice for descriptive rows.

REGION ANCHORS (every region has >=1 authority): BACK = LibreTexts 10.6 + Physiopedia lat + TeachMeAnatomy upper-limb hub; CHEST = Kenhub pec major + LibreTexts 10.6; SHOULDERS = LibreTexts 10.6 + StatPearls shoulder; ARMS = TeachMeAnatomy upper-arm + LibreTexts 10.6; FOREARMS = TeachMeAnatomy ant/post forearm (incl. FDS/FDP grip-crush group for left-pinky constraint); CORE = OpenStax 11.4 + LibreTexts 10.5; LEGS = OpenStax 11.6 + Kenhub hip/thigh + TeachMeAnatomy ant-thigh/hamstrings/gluteal + ExRx hamstrings.

CONTESTED-CLAIM COVERAGE (all six PLAN claims have >=1 primary + supporting/contradicting where applicable): lat regionalization = PMC11057623 (supports) + PMC12452428 (nuance/limits); RF active insufficiency = PLoS PMC pone.0034269 + StatPearls RF + PMC8191471; soleus-vs-gastroc knee-angle = PMC10753835 (RCT) + PMC4471746 (moment-arm) + PMC8191471; biceps long-vs-short = PMC3737788; triceps long-head overhead = Tandf Maeo 2023; hamstring biceps-femoris regional = PMC9362892. Mechanistic backbone = PMC12283864 (moment-arm systematic review, T0) + PMC2277231 (length-tension) + PMC9681132 (two-joint model).

sources.title: 11.4 Axial Muscles of the Abdominal Wall and Thorax — Anatomy and Physiology 2e (OpenStax)
sources.notes: OpenStax CC BY textbook. Core/axial muscle rows: rectus abdominis, external/internal obliques, transversus abdominis, diaphragm, intercostals with origin/insertion/movement tables. Anchor authority for the CORE region enumeration.

sources.title: 11.1 Interactions of Skeletal Muscles, Fascicle Arrangement, and Lever Systems — Anatomy and Physiology 2e (OpenStax)
sources.notes: Backs the kinesiology concepts rows: agonist/antagonist/synergist/fixator roles, origin vs insertion, lever classes/mechanical advantage. Foundational muscle-action vocabulary the antagonist-pairing concept reuses.

sources.title: 11.6 Appendicular Muscles of the Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs — Anatomy and Physiology 2e (OpenStax)
sources.notes: OpenStax CC BY. Anchor for LEGS enumeration: quads/hamstrings/glutes/adductors/calf origins, insertions, joint actions; anterior vs posterior compartment grouping.

sources.title: The Roles of Agonists, Antagonists, and Synergists — Anatomy & Physiology 2e (Oregon State, OpenStax-derived)
sources.notes: CC BY OpenStax-derived explainer of prime mover/antagonist/synergist/fixator. Second independent authority for the antagonist-pairing concept used in antagonist-of edges.

sources.title: 10.5 Axial Muscles of the Abdominal Wall and Thorax — Human Anatomy (OERI), Medicine LibreTexts
sources.notes: CC BY OER. Abdominal-wall + thoracic tables WITH innervation (adds quadratus lumborum vs OpenStax 11.4). Complements OpenStax by supplying nerve supply for CORE rows.

sources.title: 10.6 Appendicular Muscles of the Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs — Human Anatomy (OERI), Medicine LibreTexts
sources.notes: CC BY OER with full upper-limb tables incl. innervation: deltoid, rotator cuff, biceps/triceps, forearm flexors/extensors. Anchor authority for BACK/CHEST/SHOULDERS/ARMS/FOREARMS origin-insertion-action-innervation.

sources.title: Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Muscles — StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf)
sources.notes: Peer-reviewed StatPearls overview of shoulder/upper-limb musculature (attachments, innervation, function). StatPearls content is copyrighted (not OA-redistributable) — cite metadata + paraphrase only.

sources.title: Anatomy, Abdomen and Pelvis, Rectus Femoris Muscle — StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf)
sources.notes: Authoritative anatomy reference for the rectus femoris biarticular row: origin/insertion + active-insufficiency mechanism (weak knee extender when hip flexed). Backs the RF length_bias claim. Copyrighted, paraphrase only.

sources.title: Upper Limb Muscles — Shoulder, Arm, Forearm and Hand (TeachMeAnatomy)
sources.notes: Regional hub enumerating all upper-limb muscles with attachment/innervation/action tables; useful as a completeness checklist for ARMS/SHOULDERS/BACK upper-limb rows. Proprietary — paraphrase only.

sources.title: Anterior Forearm Flexor Muscles — Anatomy & Innervation (TeachMeAnatomy)
sources.notes: Per-muscle data for the wrist-flexor / finger-flexor (FDS/FDP grip-crush) group flagged for the left-pinky constraint: pronator teres, FCR, palmaris longus, FCU, FDS, FDP, FPL, pronator quadratus.

sources.title: Posterior Forearm Extensor Muscles — Anatomy & Innervation (TeachMeAnatomy)
sources.notes: Wrist-extensor group rows: ECRL/ECRB/ECU, extensor digitorum, supinator, abductor/extensor pollicis, radial-nerve innervation. Antagonist counterpart to the anterior-forearm flexor group.

sources.title: Muscles of the Upper Arm (TeachMeAnatomy)
sources.notes: Biceps brachii (biarticular: flexes shoulder+elbow, supinates), brachialis, coracobrachialis, triceps brachii heads — joints-crossed and length_bias reference for the ARMS elbow flexor/extensor rows.

sources.title: Muscles of the Gluteal Region — Superficial & Deep (TeachMeAnatomy)
sources.notes: Glute max/medius/minimus, TFL, deep lateral rotators with origin/insertion/innervation/action. Replaces the redundant per-muscle glute-max pages (Kenhub covers glute max single-muscle separately).

sources.title: Muscles of the Anterior Thigh — Quadriceps (TeachMeAnatomy)
sources.notes: Quadriceps (rectus femoris + 3 vasti), sartorius, iliopsoas, pectineus: attachments, femoral-nerve innervation, knee-extension/hip-flexion actions. LEGS quad-group enumeration.

sources.title: Muscles of the Posterior Thigh — Hamstrings (TeachMeAnatomy)
sources.notes: Biceps femoris (long+short heads), semitendinosus, semimembranosus: ischial-tuberosity origin, sciatic (tibial/peroneal) innervation, hip-extension/knee-flexion biarticular actions.

sources.title: Hip and thigh muscles: Anatomy and functions (Kenhub)
sources.notes: Comprehensive origin/insertion/innervation/action charts for hip + thigh incl. biarticular rectus femoris and hamstrings and the adductor group (magnus/longus/brevis/gracilis/pectineus). Kenhub anchor for LEGS. Proprietary — metadata + paraphrase only.

sources.title: Pectoralis major: Origin, insertion, innervation, function (Kenhub)
sources.notes: Clavicular/sternocostal/abdominal heads, intertubercular-sulcus insertion, medial+lateral pectoral nerves, adduction/internal-rotation/flexion. Backs the CHEST per-head split rows.

sources.title: Gastrocnemius muscle: Origin, insertion, functions (Kenhub)
sources.notes: Medial/lateral femoral-condyle heads, calcaneal-tendon insertion, tibial nerve, biarticular plantarflexion + knee flexion (triceps surae). Backs gastroc knee-straight length_bias row.

sources.title: Latissimus Dorsi Muscle — Physiopedia
sources.notes: Thoracolumbar/spinous-process origins, intertubercular-groove insertion, thoracodorsal nerve, shoulder extension/adduction/internal rotation. Anchor for the lat row + regionalization claim context. Physiopedia is CC BY-NC-SA but treat as reference-only.

sources.title: Hamstrings — ExRx.net Muscle Directory
sources.notes: Exercise-science muscle→exercise mapping for the biarticular hamstring group (hip-extension/knee-flexion actions and the lifts that train them). ExRx is proprietary — paraphrase only.

sources.title: Anatomical terms of motion (Wikipedia)
sources.notes: CC BY-SA canonical action vocabulary (flexion/extension, abduction/adduction, rotation, circumduction) across planes/axes. Freezes the primary_actions[] verb list as a concepts entry.

sources.title: Biarticular muscle (Wikipedia)
sources.notes: CC BY-SA definition of two-joint muscles with lower-limb examples (rectus femoris, hamstrings, gastrocnemius) and active/passive insufficiency. Backs the biarticular concept row.

sources.title: Active and Passive Insufficiency (Physiopedia)
sources.notes: Practitioner explainer of active/passive insufficiency with hamstring/rectus-femoris/finger-flexor examples. Backs the active-insufficiency concept feeding length_bias for biarticular rows.

sources.title: Muscle Moment Arm–Joint Angle Relations in the Hip, Knee, and Ankle: A Visualization of Datasets (Ann Biomed Eng 2025)
sources.notes: Systematic review compiling ~300 moment-arm datasets; moment-arm vs joint-angle curves for hip/knee/ankle muscles. CC BY 4.0. Mechanistic backbone for joint-angle length_bias claims across the lower limb.

sources.title: Roles of Mono- and Bi-articular Muscles in Human Limbs: Two-joint Link Model and Applications (Integr Org Biol 2022)
sources.notes: CC BY review of the two-joint link model — how mono/biarticular muscles coordinate force direction at the limb endpoint. Replaces the 403/unknown-license Royal Society Interface biarticular review.

sources.title: Novel Insights Into Biarticular Muscle Actions Gained From High-Density Electromyogram (Exerc Sport Sci Rev 2021)
sources.notes: CC BY 4.0 (license confirmed via fetch). Region-specific activation of biarticular rectus femoris/gastrocnemius — proximal regions favor hip action, distal favor knee action. Backs RF and gastroc regional length_bias.

sources.title: Understanding muscle from its length (PMC)
sources.notes: PMC OA review of the length-tension relationship, active vs passive tension, filament overlap and titin. Core mechanism row behind length-dependent force / length_bias concept.

sources.title: Task-Dependent Inhomogeneous Muscle Activities within the Bi-Articular Human Rectus Femoris Muscle (Miyamoto et al. 2012, PLoS ONE)
sources.notes: CC BY primary regional EMG: distal RF cannot be fully activated during hip flexion vs knee extension — direct evidence for the rectus-femoris active-insufficiency claim.

sources.title: Triceps surae hypertrophy greater after standing vs seated calf-raise training (Kinoshita et al. 2023, Front Physiol)
sources.notes: CC BY RCT: standing (knee-extended) grows gastroc far more, seated (knee-flexed) similar soleus. Primary trial settling the gastroc-knee-straight vs soleus-knee-bent length_bias claim.

sources.title: Knee and Ankle Joint Angles Influence the Plantarflexion Torque of the Gastrocnemius (PMC)
sources.notes: CC OA: gastroc plantarflexion torque vs knee+ankle angle; gastroc contributes >=40% torque at straight knee. Moment-arm/length mechanism for the soleus-vs-gastroc knee-angle independence claim.

sources.title: High-Density EMG Excitation in Front vs Back Lat Pull-Down Prime Movers (J Hum Kinet 2024)
sources.notes: CC BY HD-sEMG: front vs back pulldown produce different lat excitation/phase-dependent engagement. Primary evidence for the lat-regionalization claim (bias by arm path).

sources.title: EMG of Back Muscle Activation During Lat Pulldown: Grip Variations and Forearm Orientation (J Funct Morphol Kinesiol 2025)
sources.notes: CC BY: 7 grip variants in 40 trained men show no significant LD-activation difference across grips. Counterpoint/nuance that constrains the lat-regionalization claim (grip width does NOT target lat regions).

sources.title: Triceps brachii hypertrophy substantially greater after elbow extension training in overhead vs neutral arm position (Maeo et al. 2023, Eur J Sport Sci)
sources.notes: Primary RCT in trained subjects: overhead (lengthened long head) yields ~1.4x greater triceps growth than neutral. Backs the triceps-long-head-overhead-stretch length_bias claim. Tandfonline — license unconfirmed, treat as reference-only.

sources.title: Effect of shoulder position on biceps brachii EMG in different dumbbell curls (Oliveira et al., PMC)
sources.notes: CC OA primary EMG: shoulder position (extended vs flexed) modulates biceps EMG via long-head length. Basis for the incline (long-head bias) vs preacher (short-head) length_bias claim.

sources.title: Muscle Activation Patterns of Proximal/Distal Biceps Femoris and Gluteus Maximus Across Hip-Extension and Knee-Flexion Exercises in Trained Women (PMC)
sources.notes: CC OA EMG (trained women): region-specific biceps femoris and glute-max activation across hip-extension vs knee-flexion exercises. Backs the hamstring biarticular hip-extensor-vs-knee-flexor regional claim.
